mainTopic: When is מין במינו בטל according to רבי יהודה, and do we check the מבטל (רב חסדא) or the בטל (רבי חנינא)?
overview: The גמרא wants to know which opinion stands behind רב חסדא and רבי חנינא, who argue about mixtures of נבילה and שחוטה. It bases them on רבי חייא's teaching that נבילה and שחוטה are בטל in each other. It then reads רבי יהודה this way: מין במינו is not בטל only when one item can actually become like the other. רב חסדא checks whether the larger item (the מבטל) can become like the smaller one. רבי חנינא checks whether the smaller item (the בטל) can become like the larger one. The גמרא tests both views against several cases in the משנה about mixed מנחות, קומץ, and שירים. Each time, it answers with רבי זירא's rule: since הקטרה is said about both the קומץ and the שירים, they do not cancel each other. A ברייתא about seasoned מצה is also deflected: it speaks of a mixture that is mostly מצה. A new story then begins, in which רב כהנא hears the sons of רבי חייא discussing a divided עשרון; that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה judges by appearance, so this attempt fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea of basing the discussion on רבי יהודה. He goes by how things look, and נבילה and שחוטה look alike, so they count as מין במינו, which he says is not בטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה goes by appearance, and both this and that are the same kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on an earlier attempt to explain the opinions using רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, what makes two things 'the same kind' is how they look. Meat from a נבילה and meat from a שחוטה look exactly alike, so for him they are מין במינו. He holds that מין במינו is never בטל, so his view cannot be the basis for saying one is בטל in the other.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes by the appearance (how the item looks)
A substance mixed with the same kind of substance
Both this one and that one

steps.confusionAlert: Even though נבילה and שחוטה are very different in halacha, for רבי יהודה they still count as the 'same kind', because they look the same.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda follows the appearance,
and this and that are a substance with its own kind.
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means the meat of the נבילה and the meat of the שחוטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects an earlier attempt, from before this section, to base the dispute on רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole attempt to base the opinions of רב חסדא and רבי חנינא on רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For רבי יהודה, appearance decides the type. נבילה and שחוטה look identical, so they are מין במינו and cannot be בטל.

steps.title: A new basis: the ברייתא of רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: Instead, the גמרא says the opinions follow רבי חייא, who teaches that נבילה and שחוטה are בטל in each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows רבי חייא. רבי חייא taught: נבילה and שחוטה cancel each other out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new source for the opinions it is trying to explain: a teaching of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא says outright that נבילה and שחוטה can be בטל in each other. This gives a clear base for saying that one of them disappears in a majority of the other.

keyTerms.meaning: According to (someone's opinion)
An animal that died without proper שחיטה; its meat is forbidden
An animal that was properly slaughtered
They cancel each other out (each can be nullified in the other)

phrases.english: Rather, it is according to Rabbi Chiya,
as Rabbi Chiya teaches:
An animal carcass and a slaughtered animal are nullified one in the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי יהודה as the base, offers רבי חייא instead.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifting the source of the opinions to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The opinions were based on רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are based on רבי חייא's ruling that נבילה and שחוטה are בטל in each other.

steps.title: Whose view does Rabbi Chiya follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion רבי חייא follows. It does not seem to fit the רבנן, and it does not seem to fit רבי יהודה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא follows whom? If he follows the רבנן, they said that only things offered on the altar don't cancel each other, which means that otherwise מין במינו is בטל. And if he follows רבי יהודה, then for רבי יהודה every מין במינו is never בטל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא's ruling by testing it against both known opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא and רבי חנינא each read רבי חייא as saying that in one direction the meat is not בטל. Under the רבנן, any מין במינו is בטל (only עולין are an exception), so there is no room for a case that is not בטל. Under רבי יהודה, מין במינו is never בטל, and נבילה and שחוטה count as the same kind, so there is no room for a case that is בטל. Either way, the ruling as they read it fits neither side.

keyTerms.meaning: Items that go up on the מזבח (altar)
Each other
Is nullified, cancelled out in the majority

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya is according to whom?
If according to the Rabbis,
didn't they say:
it is items that go up on the altar that do not nullify each other,
which implies that otherwise, a substance with its own kind is nullified!
And if according to Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִין בְּמִינוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֹא בָּטֵיל!
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yehuda, any substance with its own kind is not nullified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new basis offered in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's ruling that נבילה and שחוטה are בטל in each other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided trap. Under the רבנן, all מין במינו (except עולין) is בטל, so there is no direction in which the meat is not בטל, as רב חסדא and רבי חנינא require. Under רבי יהודה, nothing of the same kind is ever בטל, so the ruling that they are בטל contradicts him.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's rule only applies when one can become like the other
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא follows רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה's rule that מין במינו is not בטל applies only when one item can become like the other. Where that is impossible, it is בטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he follows רבי יהודה. When רבי יהודה said that מין במינו is not בטל, that is only where one can become like the other. But where it cannot become like the other, it is בטל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Looking the same is not enough for רבי יהודה's rule to apply. The two items must also be able to actually turn into one another. If one cannot become like the other, they are not truly 'the same kind', so even רבי יהודה agrees that the item is בטל.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (the גמרא sticks with an option it had seemed to reject)
These words apply only (to this case)
It is possible for it to become like the other

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, מין במינו is not בטל only when one item can become like the other. When that is impossible, even he agrees it is בטל. This is how רבי חייא's ruling fits רבי יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This adds a new condition for what counts as 'the same kind' (מין במינו). Appearance alone is not enough; the items must also be able to become like each other.

phrases.english: Actually, it is according to Rabbi Yehuda,
and when Rabbi Yehuda says:
a substance with its own kind is not nullified,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּאֶפְשָׁר לֵיהּ לְמִיהְוֵי כְּוָותֵיהּ,
phrases.english: that applies only where it is possible for it to become like the other,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר לֵיהּ לְמִיהְוֵי כְּוָותֵיהּ – בָּטֵל.
phrases.english: but where it is not possible for it to become like the other, it is nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by choosing the רבי יהודה side and limiting his rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבי יהודה's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי יהודה, any two items that look alike are never בטל in each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: His rule applies only when one item can become like the other. Otherwise the item is בטל, which fits רבי חייא's ruling.

steps.title: What exactly רב חסדא and רבי חנינא disagree about
steps.stepSummary: Both agree with רבי חייא's reading of רבי יהודה: מין במינו is not בטל only when one item can become like the other. They disagree about which item we check. רב חסדא checks the larger item (מבטל). רבי חנינא checks the smaller item (בטל).
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the point of their disagreement. רב חסדא holds that we go after the item that does the nullifying. רבי חנינא holds that we go after the item that gets nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now pins down the exact point that רב חסדא and רבי חנינא argue about, building on the rule from Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said מין במינו is not בטל only if one item can turn into the other. Now we learn the dispute is about which direction counts. רב חסדא asks whether the larger amount can become like the smaller one. רבי חנינא asks whether the smaller amount can become like the larger one.

keyTerms.meaning: The nullifier, meaning the larger amount that could cancel out the smaller one
The nullified item, meaning the smaller amount that might get cancelled out
We go after, meaning this is the thing we look at to decide
They disagree

steps.confusionAlert: Both אמוראים use the same basic rule: no ביטול if one item can become like the other. They only argue about which item we check, the big one or the small one.

phrases.english: And in this they disagree:
phrases.notes: "They" means רב חסדא and רבי חנינא, whose argument about נבילה and שחוטה came earlier.

phrases.english: For Rav Chisda holds:
we go after the nullifying item.
phrases.notes: He means we check whether the bigger amount can become like the smaller one.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina holds:
we go after the nullified item.
phrases.notes: Here we check whether the smaller amount can become like the bigger one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule from Step 4 (no ביטול only where one item can become the other) to explain the dispute between רב חסדא and רבי חנינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא: check whether the מבטל can become like the בטל. רבי חנינא: check whether the בטל can become like the מבטל.

steps.title: Proof for רבי חנינא from two mixed meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that if two מנחות got mixed before קמיצה, they stay כשרות as long as a קמיצה can be taken from each one separately. Once the first one's קמיצה is taken, its leftover becomes שירים. Yet the שירים do not nullify the second מנחה, which still needs its קמיצה. The second מנחה (the בטל) can later become שירים, so it is not בטל. That fits רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: two meal offerings that had no handful removed yet got mixed together. If the כהן can take a handful from each one on its own, they are fit. If not, they are unfit. Now here, once he takes the handful from one, the rest of that one becomes שירים. And still the שירים do not nullify the other meal offering that has not had its handful taken yet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support רבי חנינא's view that we look at the nullified item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the first קמיצה, the mixture holds two different things: שירים (the larger amount, the מבטל) and an untouched מנחה (the בטל). The untouched מנחה can become שירים once its own קמיצה is taken, but שירים can never go back to needing קמיצה. Since the משנה treats the second מנחה as not בטל, what counts is whether the בטל can become the מבטל. That is רבי חנינא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offerings made of flour and oil
Having the קֹמֶץ (handful) removed, the part of the מנחה burned on the מזבח
The leftover of a מנחה after the handful is removed, eaten by the כהנים
A מנחה whose handful has not been taken yet, compared to טֶבֶל (produce before its gifts are separated)
Fit / unfit to be offered

steps.whyThisMatters: This ראיה only works if the משנה holds that מין במינו is not בטל. The next two steps check that before the proof can stand.

phrases.english: We learned: two meal offerings from which a handful was not removed
and they got mixed with each other,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יָכוֹל לִקְמוֹץ מִזּוֹ בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ
phrases.english: if he can take a handful from this one by itself
and from that one by itself, they are fit,
and if not, they are unfit.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּקָמֵיץ לֵיהּ מֵחֲדָא –
phrases.english: But here, once he takes the handful from one,
the rest of it becomes שירים,
and the שירים do not nullify the one still needing its handful.
phrases.notes: טיבלא literally means "untithed." Here it's the second מנחה, since its handful hasn't been taken yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to back up רבי חנינא's side of the dispute set out in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's view that we follow the בטל (the smaller item).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of two מנחות mixed before קמיצה: the שירים do not nullify the untouched מנחה, which can itself become שירים.

steps.title: Which תנא wrote this משנה? Not the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows. It cannot be the רבנן. They hold that only things going up on the מזבח (עולין) do not nullify each other, but ordinary מין במינו is בטל. שירים are eaten, not put on the מזבח, so by the רבנן the second מנחה should be בטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If it is the רבנן, they say that only items that go up on the מזבח do not nullify each other. That means a substance mixed with its own kind is nullified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whose view the משנה follows. This is needed to show the proof in Step 6 really works, and it sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only holds if the משנה believes that מין במינו is normally not בטל. The רבנן say מין במינו is בטל, except for עולין. Here the שירים are not עולין and both items are flour and oil, so by the רבנן the second מנחה would be lost. So the משנה cannot follow the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Which תנא does this follow?
Items that go up on the מזבח
A substance mixed with the same kind of substance
Each other

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
If the רבנן, don't they say:
it is only items going up on the altar that do not nullify each other,
which means a substance mixed with its own kind is nullified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests whether the משנה used as proof in Step 6 can follow the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the משנה follows, and whether he holds that מין במינו is not בטל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן hold that מין במינו is בטל except for עולין. שירים are not עולין, so the second מנחה would be בטל, which contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: The משנה must follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Since it cannot be the רבנן, the משנה clearly follows רבי יהודה, who holds that מין במינו is not בטל. Following רבי חייא's reading of רבי יהודה, the משנה then shows that we look at the בטל, like רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that מין במינו is not בטל, but only where one item can become the other (Step 4). The second מנחה is not בטל because it can become שירים. So the proof for רבי חנינא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it is obvious

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה of two mixed מנחות follows רבי יהודה. The untouched מנחה is not בטל in the שירים because it can become שירים, though שירים can't become it. This supports רבי חנינא: we follow the בטל.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious: רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7 by assigning the משנה to רבי יהודה, which completes the proof from Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds that מין במינו is not בטל, so it can serve as a proof for רבי חנינא's view of how רבי יהודה's rule works.

steps.title: Setup: the משנה fits רבי חנינא easily
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי חנינא, who checks the בטל, the משנה is simple. The second מנחה will itself become שירים once its קמיצה is taken, so it is not בטל in the first one's שירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says we look at the item that might be nullified. That item can become like the nullifying item, because once the קמיצה is taken from the other מנחה, it too becomes שירים just like these.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It first says how well the משנה fits רבי חנינא, so it can next ask how רב חסדא would explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the first מנחה's leftover (שירים) is mixed with the second מנחה, which still needs its קמיצה. By רבי חנינא we check the smaller item, the second מנחה. It can later become שירים too, so by רבי יהודה's rule it is not בטל. This is the 'easy side' before the difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for this view). It opens a contrast: 'but for the other view...'
We go after the item that might be nullified (the smaller part)
Like the item that does the nullifying (the larger part)
He takes the קומץ (handful) from a מנחה

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says:
we go after the item that is nullified,
phrases.notes: This is רבי חנינא from Step 5.

phrases.english: the nullified item can become like the nullifying item,
for when he takes the handful from the other one,
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is the second מנחה, the one mixed into the first one's leftover.

phrases.english: it becomes leftover just like these.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר בָּטֵל אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats why the משנה fits רבי חנינא (Steps 6 and 8), as the first half of a בשלמא/אלא challenge.

steps.title: How would רב חסדא explain the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: By רב חסדא we check the מבטל, the שירים. שירים can never turn back into a מנחה that still needs קמיצה. So must we say that, by רב חסדא, the משנה does not fit רבי חייא?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says we look at the nullifying item, can שירים ever become an untreated מנחה? Shall we say that according to רב חסדא, the משנה is not like רבי חייא?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the challenge itself. The משנה seems to go against רב חסדא, unless he says the משנה does not follow רבי חייא's reading of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רב חסדא we look at the larger item, the שירים. שירים cannot go back to being a מנחה before קמיצה, so by רבי חייא's rule the second מנחה should be בטל. Yet the משנה says it is not בטל. So רב חסדא seems forced to say the משנה disagrees with רבי חייא, which is a hard position to hold.

keyTerms.meaning: We go after the nullifying item (the larger part)
Like טבל: something that still needs a required portion taken from it. Here, a מנחה whose קמיצה was not yet taken.
Shall we say? It brings up a suggestion the גמרא would rather avoid.
According to the view of

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
we go after the nullifying item,
can leftover ever become an untreated מנחה?
phrases.notes: He means a מנחה that still needs its קמיצה taken, like produce that still needs its tithes.

phrases.english: Shall we say that according to רב חסדא,
the משנה is not like רבי חייא?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר מְבַטֵּל אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא/אלא: what is easy for רבי חנינא is hard for רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that we check the מבטל, together with רבי חייא's reading of רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שירים (מבטל) can never become a מנחה before קמיצה. By רבי חייא, the second מנחה should then be בטל, but the משנה says it is not. So רב חסדא would have to reject רבי חייא.

steps.title: The משנה rests on רבי זירא's special rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's ruling does not come from the general rule of מין במינו. It comes from רבי זירא's comparison: הקטרה is said about both the קומץ and the שירים. Just as one קומץ does not nullify another, שירים do not nullify a קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is like רבי זירא. He said: 'burning' is said about the קומץ, and 'burning' is said about the שירים. Just as with the קומץ, one קומץ does not nullify another, so too with the שירים, the שירים do not nullify the קומץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב חסדא. The משנה has a special reason from a פסוק, so it is not a proof about which item we check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא links the קומץ and the שירים because the תורה uses the word הקטרה for both. Two קמצים never nullify each other. So the שירים also cannot nullify the second מנחה, which still has its קומץ to be taken. That rule is special to מנחות, so the משנה tells us nothing about the רב חסדא and רבי חנינא argument. The proof for רבי חנינא falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that case (the משנה of the mixed מנחות)
Burning on the מזבח
The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
Learning a law from the same word used in two places in the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה of the mixed מנחות is not a proof for רבי חנינא. Its ruling comes from רבי זירא's rule that שירים, like a קומץ, do not nullify a קומץ. רב חסדא can still hold with רבי חייא.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי זירא is talking about the general rule of מין במינו. His rule is special to קומץ and שירים, and that is exactly why the משנה can no longer settle the general argument.
steps.whyThisMatters: It saves רב חסדא's view. It also shows that a case with its own special reason cannot be used to prove a general rule.

phrases.english: There, it follows רבי זירא,
for רבי זירא said:
'burning' is said about the handful,
and 'burning' is said about the leftover.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:11. Here the word comes in a ban on burning, but it is the same word.

phrases.english: Just as with the burning said about the handful,
one handful does not nullify another,
so too with the burning said about the leftover,
the leftover does not nullify the handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10 by giving the משנה a separate, special source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the case its own special reason, so the משנה is not about the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's ruling came from רבי יהודה's general rule, so it would prove we look at the בטל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's ruling comes from רבי זירא's גזירה שוה linking קומץ and שירים, so it fits רב חסדא as well.

steps.title: A new case: a קומץ mixed into a מנחה not yet נקמצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case of the משנה. A קומץ mixed into a מנחה whose קומץ was not yet taken is not בטל in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If a קומץ got mixed into a מנחה whose קומץ was not yet taken, the כהן should not burn it. If he did burn it, the מנחה whose קומץ was taken counts for its owner. The one whose קומץ was not taken does not count. So the unfinished מנחה does not cancel out the קומץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case from the משנה to test the same question as before. It is setting up the next round of 'whose view is this?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning the mixture counts for the first מנחה. That means its קומץ was really burned and was not swallowed up by the unfinished מנחה. So here a קומץ is not בטל in a whole מנחה, and the גמרא will ask what rule explains that.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
A מנחה whose קומץ has not yet been taken
The unfinished מנחה that still needs its קומץ taken
It counts for the owner and fulfills his obligation
Cancels out, makes something else נבטל

phrases.english: Come and hear: the handful that got mixed
into a meal offering whose handful was not taken – he should not burn it,
but if he burned it –
this one, whose handful was taken, counts for the owner,

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִקְמְצָה לֹא עָלְתָה לַבְּעָלִים,
phrases.english: and that one, whose handful was not taken, does not count for the owner,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא קָא מְבַטֵּיל לֵיהּ טִיבְלָא לְקוֹמֶץ.
phrases.english: so the untaken meal offering does not nullify the handful.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַקּוֹמֶץ שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בְּמִנְחָה שֶׁלֹּא נִקְמְצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of שירים and a מנחה to a parallel case: a קומץ and an unfinished מנחה.
steps.raayaObject: That a קומץ is not בטל in a מנחה whose קומץ was not yet taken
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that burning the mixture counts for the מנחה whose קומץ was taken

steps.title: Whose view is it? It cannot be the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view this case follows. The רבנן would say ordinary מין במינו is בטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If it is the רבנן, they say only things that go up on the מזבח don't cancel each other out, but ordinary same-kind mixtures are בטל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion this case follows and shows it cannot be the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the רבנן, only עולין, two things that are both burned on the מזבח, are not בטל. The unfinished מנחה is not itself burned as is, so by the רבנן this is plain מין במינו, and the קומץ should be בטל.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is it?
Items that go up on the מזבח
Each other
A substance mixed with its own kind is nullified (the רבנן's general view)

phrases.english: Whose view is it? If it is the Rabbis –
but they say:
it is items that go up on the altar that do not nullify one another,
but a substance with its own kind is nullified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose view the newly quoted case follows, the same way step 7 did for the earlier case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the case of the קומץ in an unfinished מנחה follows

steps.title: It must be רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Since the רבנן don't fit, the case clearly follows רבי יהודה, who says מין במינו is not בטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious: it is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: this case follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that any substance mixed with its own kind is not בטל. The קומץ and the unfinished מנחה are both flour of a מנחה, so by him the קומץ survives the mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
A substance mixed with its own kind is not nullified (רבי יהודה's view)

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious – it is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case follows רבי יהודה, who holds מין במינו לא בטל.

steps.title: By רב חסדא the case works easily
steps.stepSummary: If we look at the מבטל (רב חסדא), the case works. Every bit of the unfinished מנחה could still become a קומץ, so it counts as the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says we follow the מבטל. The מבטל can become like the בטל, since every bit of the מנחה is fit to have a קומץ taken from it. So it is מין במינו, and מין במינו is not בטל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the case fits nicely by רב חסדא. It is setting up the difficulty that will come for the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא checks the מבטל, here the unfinished מנחה. Any part of it could still be taken as a קומץ, so it can turn into the same thing as the קומץ it is mixed with. That makes it truly מין במינו, so by רבי יהודה the קומץ is not בטל.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for… (opens a contrast)
We follow the nullifying substance (רב חסדא)
A small bit
To take a קומץ from

steps.confusionAlert: Careful: this is the reverse of steps 9 and 10! There רבי חנינא was the easy view and רב חסדא was hard. Here רב חסדא is easy and רבי חנינא is hard.

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says:
we follow the nullifying substance,
the nullifying substance can become like the nullified one,
since every bit of it is fit to have the handful taken from it,
so it is a substance with its own kind,
and a substance with its own kind is not nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: בָּתַר מְבַטֵּל אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the רבי יהודה reading against רב חסדא's view and finds it fits.
steps.kashyaTarget: Sets up the challenge against רבי חנינא's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Shows the case only fits easily when we look at the מבטל, setting up the problem for the view that looks at the בטל.

steps.title: By רבי חנינא: can a קומץ become an unfinished מנחה?
steps.stepSummary: If we look at the בטל (רבי חנינא), the קומץ can never become an unfinished מנחה. So must the משנה disagree with רבי חייא?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the one who says we follow the בטל, can a קומץ become an unfinished מנחה? Shall we say this does not fit רבי חייא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא's view. It asks whether the משנה must then go against רבי חייא's reading of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא checks the בטל, here the קומץ. A קומץ is finished and can never turn back into a מנחה that still needs its קומץ taken. So the two are not the same kind, and by this view the קומץ should be בטל. The ruling seems to clash with רבי חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: We follow the nullified substance (רבי חנינא)
Can it become…? (a challenge expecting 'no')
Shall we say…? (a suggestion the גמרא may reject)

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
we follow the nullified substance,
can a handful become an untaken meal offering?
Shall we say it is not in line with Rabbi Ḥiyya?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר בָּטֵל אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא… אלא contrast that step 15 opened.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's view that we look at the בטל, together with רבי חייא's reading of רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קומץ can never turn back into an unfinished מנחה, so by looking at the בטל it is not מין במינו. Yet the משנה rules it is not בטל.

steps.title: This case also comes from רבי זירא's comparison
steps.stepSummary: The answer: this ruling also follows רבי זירא. Because of the comparison of הקטרה, a קומץ is not cancelled by a מנחה, not because of the rule of מין במינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case too follows רבי זירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge the same way it did in step 11: this ruling comes from רבי זירא's special comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ is not בטל here because of the comparison based on הקטרה, not because of the general rule of מין במינו. So the question of whether the בטל can change into the מבטל does not matter. רבי חנינא stays in line with רבי חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: This one too
Burning on the מזבח, the shared word behind רבי זירא's comparison

steps.whatToRemember: Both cases of the משנה, שירים with a מנחה and a קומץ with an unfinished מנחה, are explained by רבי זירא's comparison. That way neither רב חסדא nor רבי חנינא is forced to disagree with רבי חייא.

phrases.english: This too is like Rabbi Zeira.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 11: הקטרה is said about both the קומץ and the שירים, so they don't cancel each other out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by reusing the solution from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the source of the ruling from a general rule to a special comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling depends on מין במינו, so רבי חנינא's view would clash with רבי חייא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling comes from רבי זירא's comparison of הקטרה, so there is no clash.

steps.title: A handful mixed into another offering's leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a case from the משנה where a קומץ got mixed into the שירים of a different מנחה. Even though neither part can ever turn into the other, the שירים do not cancel the קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if the handful got mixed into the leftovers of another meal offering, the כהן should not burn it. But if he did burn it, the offering counts for the owner. Here the leftovers can never become a handful, and the handful can never become leftovers, and still the leftovers do not cancel the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case to test רבי חייא's rule about when something is cancelled. In this case neither part can turn into the other, yet the קומץ is not cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is worded so it is strong against רבי חייא. The שירים can never become a קומץ, and the קומץ can never become שירים. If the קומץ still is not cancelled, this seems to go against the idea that such a mixture should be בטל.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour the כהן takes out of a מנחה and burns on the מזבח
The leftover part of a מנחה after the קומץ is taken out; the כהנים eat it
It counts for the owner; his obligation is done
The part that does the cancelling, usually the bigger amount
The part that gets cancelled and loses its own identity

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If its handful got mixed into the leftovers of another meal offering,
he should not burn it,
and if he did burn it, it counts for the owner.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא דְּלָא הָוֵי מְבַטֵּל כְּבָטֵיל,
phrases.english: But here, the cancelling part cannot become like the cancelled part,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא קָא מְבַטְּלִי לֵיהּ שִׁירַיִם לְקוֹמֶץ.
phrases.english: and yet the leftovers do not cancel the handful.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִתְעָרֵב קוּמְצָהּ בְּשִׁירַיִם שֶׁל חֲבֶרְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering the first case with רבי זירא, the גמרא brings a second case from the משנה that tests רבי חייא again.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's rule about when something can be cancelled in a mixture
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Neither part can become the other, which should allow ביטול, yet the משנה says the קומץ is not cancelled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קומץ mixed into another מנחה's שירים should not be burned, but if it was burned the offering counts.

steps.title: Whose view does this case follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again whose view this ruling fits, using the same reasoning it used for the earlier case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If the רבנן, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats, in short form, the same question it asked about the earlier case. The word וכו׳ tells us to fill in the whole argument from before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full argument is: the רבנן say regular מין במינו is cancelled, so this must be רבי יהודה. But then it seems that for רבי יהודה the קומץ is NOT cancelled even though neither part can become the other. That goes against רבי חייא, who says that in such a case the item is בטל. The next step answers this with רבי זירא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
And so on; fill in the rest from earlier
A substance mixed with the same kind of substance

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
If the Rabbis, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the new case into the same question about whose view it follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא this משנה follows, and whether that view clashes with רבי חייא.

steps.title: רבי זירא's comparison of burning again
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that this case is a special rule. Since the תורה says 'burning' about both the קומץ and the שירים, the שירים cannot cancel a קומץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: 'burning' is said about the handful, and 'burning' is said about the leftovers. Just as with the burning said about the handful, one handful does not cancel another, so too with the burning said about the leftovers, leftovers do not cancel a handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the same way it did before: the case is explained by רבי זירא's comparison. The קומץ is not cancelled because of a special rule from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two handfuls mixed together never cancel each other. רבי זירא links the שירים to the קומץ because the same word, הקטרה, is used for both. So the שירים get the same rule and cannot cancel a קומץ, and the case says nothing against רבי חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning on the מזבח
It was said; used here to show the same word appears in two places
Does not cancel the other one

steps.whatToRemember: A קומץ mixed into שירים is not cancelled because of רבי זירא's special rule about הקטרה, not because of the general rule of מין במינו. So this case cannot be used against רבי חייא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this proves that every mixture of the same kind stays uncancelled. The rule here comes only from the special link of הקטרה between קומץ and שירים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
'Burning' is said about the handful,
and 'burning' is said about the leftovers.
Just as with the burning said about the handful,
one handful does not cancel another,
so too with the burning said about the leftovers,
the leftovers do not cancel the handful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: נֶאֶמְרָה הַקְטָרָה בַּקּוֹמֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from steps 18-19 with the same reasoning used in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special rule from the פסוקים takes the case out of the general rules of ביטול
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case seemed to follow רבי יהודה's rule of מין במינו and clash with רבי חייא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קומץ survives because of the הקטרה comparison, so there is no clash with רבי חייא.

steps.title: A new proof from seasoned מצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: מצה seasoned with spices is still kosher מצה, just called 'seasoned מצה'. The גמרא first assumes there were more spices than מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he seasoned it with black cumin, with sesame, or with any kind of spice, it is fit. It is מצה, only it is called seasoned מצה. You might think this is a case where there were more spices than מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to prove something about ביטול in a mixture. It ends by stating its first assumption, which sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says spiced מצה is still מצה. The גמרא first understands this as a case where the spices are the bigger amount. If so, the smaller part (the מצה) keeps its identity, and the גמרא will build on this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He seasoned it
Black cumin, a seed spice
Sesame seeds
Seasoned מצה
It enters your mind; the first assumption, which may later change
There was more of it

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he seasoned it with black cumin, with sesame,
or with any kind of spice, it is fit.
It is מצה,
only it is called seasoned מצה.
You might think
that there were more spices than מצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the קומץ cases, the גמרא opens a new proof from a ברייתא about seasoned מצה.
steps.raayaObject: That we follow the בטל (רבי חנינא): the smaller amount of מצה is not cancelled by spices that can never become מצה. This sets up the challenge to רב חסדא in the next step.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that spiced מצה is still kosher מצה, assumed at first to have more spices than מצה

steps.title: Seasoned מצה fits one view but challenges the other
steps.stepSummary: The view that follows the בטל can explain why the מצה is not cancelled, since moldy מצה becomes like spices. The view that follows the מבטל has a problem, because spices can never become מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who says we follow the thing being cancelled: the cancelled thing (the מצה) can become like the cancelling thing (the spices), because when מצה gets moldy it becomes like spices. But according to the one who says we follow the cancelling thing: can spices ever become מצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא of seasoned מצה to attack the view that follows the מבטל. It assumes there are more spices than מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of מין במינו only applies if the two parts can become alike. If you look at the מצה, it can turn into something like spices once it is moldy, so the parts count as the same kind and the מצה is not cancelled. If you look at the spices, they can never become מצה, so the מצה should be cancelled. That contradicts the ברייתא, which calls it kosher מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The smaller item that might get cancelled in a mixture
The larger item that might do the cancelling
We follow / we judge by
Becomes moldy
Spices

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two words. בטל is the thing that would disappear (here the מצה). מבטל is the thing that would make it disappear (here the spices).

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
we follow the thing being cancelled,
the cancelled thing can become like the cancelling thing,
since when it gets moldy
phrases.notes: 'It' is the מצה. Moldy מצה can no longer be used for the מצוה, so it is no better than spices.

phrases.english: it becomes like spices.
phrases.notes: Some versions have הוי, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is הויא. Either way the meaning is the same.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
we follow the cancelling thing,
can spices ever become מצה?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר בָּטֵל אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא brought in step 21 and turns it into a challenge against the view that follows the מבטל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that we follow the מבטל when deciding about מין במינו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spices can never become מצה, so by this view they are not the same kind. The larger amount of spices should cancel the מצה, yet the ברייתא says it is still מצה.

steps.title: The case is where most of it is מצה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a case where there are not more spices than מצה. Most of the mixture is מצה, so the מצה is not cancelled at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where the spices are not more than the מצה. Most of it is מצה, so it is not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the view that follows the מבטל by saying the ברייתא is about a different case than we first assumed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 assumed there were more spices than מצה. Now the גמרא says the opposite: the מצה is the majority. A majority is never cancelled, so this ברייתא proves nothing about מין במינו, and neither view is challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to give a case a new, narrower setting
Was more / was the larger amount
Its majority

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by changing what case the ברייתא is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא meant there were more spices than מצה, which would be a problem for the view that follows the מבטל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means most of it is מצה, so the מצה is never cancelled and there is no proof either way.

steps.title: The wording 'seasoned מצה' supports this answer
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא calls it 'מצה, only it is called seasoned מצה'. That name shows the main part is מצה, with spices just added.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact this way, because it teaches: 'It is מצה, only it is called seasoned מצה.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer from step 23 by reading the ברייתא's own words closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the spices were the larger part, the food would not be called 'seasoned מצה'. Calling it מצה with seasoning shows that מצה is the main thing. So the ברייתא really is about a mixture that is mostly מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact / it fits closely, introducing support from the exact words
Seasoned מצה
Learn from this, meaning the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of seasoned מצה is about a mixture that is mostly מצה. So it does not decide whether we follow the בטל or the מבטל.

steps.raayaObject: The answer that the ברייתא is about a mixture that is mostly מצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's phrase 'it is called seasoned מצה', which shows מצה is the main part.

steps.title: רב כהנא hears the sons of רבי חייא discussing a divided עשרון
steps.stepSummary: A new section begins. When רב כהנא went up to ארץ ישראל, he found the sons of רבי חייא discussing the case of an עשרון that someone divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב כהנא went up to ארץ ישראל, he found the sons of רבי חייא sitting and saying: An עשרון that someone divided...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new story and setting up a new discussion. The case of the divided עשרון continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only sets the scene: who was there and what topic they raised. The actual ruling about the עשרון that was split comes next, so do not look for a conclusion here yet.
